scenario: A colleague presents your idea as their own in a meeting with your manager. Nobody else knows it was yours.

options.text: Let it go; the team benefits either way.
Tell your manager privately that it was your idea.
Stay quiet, and use it against them later.
Talk to the colleague first, before anyone else.

scenario: A cashier gives you 20 euros too much in change. You only notice once you are back at your car.

options.text: Go back and return it.
Keep it; it was their mistake.

scenario: Your best friend asks you to be their alibi: they say they were with you last night. You know they were somewhere they should not have been.

answer.prompt: How likely are you to cover for them?

scenario: Your father can no longer live alone. Moving him in would strain your relationship and your job, and the only good care home nearby would use up his savings.

options.text: Move him in, whatever it costs your job and your relationship.
Arrange daily home help and draw up a rota to check on him.
Insist that each sibling takes him in for a month in turn.
Choose the cheaper home further away; it keeps more of his savings in the family.

scenario: A runaway trolley will hit five workers. You are a passer-by next to a lever that would send it onto a side track, killing the one worker there. If you pull it, you will be the one held responsible for that death.

options.text: Pull the lever.
Do nothing.

scenario: You find a stranger's phone on a bench. It is unlocked.

answer.prompt: What do you do, in a sentence?

scenario: Your team misses a deadline because a teammate was ill. Your manager asks who is responsible.

options.text: Say the whole team shares the blame.
Explain exactly what happened, including the illness.
Point out that you delivered your part on time.
Let the ill teammate take the blame; they are not there anyway.

scenario: Your manager tells you to follow a new procedure that you think is slower than the old one.

options.text: Follow it as instructed.
Follow it, and send a short note suggesting a better way.
Quietly keep doing it your way.
Get colleagues together to push back as a group.

scenario: You win 1,000 euros in a work raffle.

options.text: Split it evenly with everyone at your table; you all bought tickets together.
Give a large part to a charity that saves lives abroad.
Spend it on a trip somewhere you have never been.
Put it all into savings.

scenario: A close friend shows you their new business plan. You are fairly sure it will fail. They ask what you honestly think.
Your friend wants to go out on a Monday night. You have an important meeting at 8 am on Tuesday.

options.text: Go. Tuesday-you can deal with it.
Say yes, then cancel at 9 pm with a mysterious headache.
Go for one drink, and actually leave after one drink.
Go, but make your friend promise to drag you home by midnight.

scenario: A colleague posts a photo of you from the team party without asking. You look fine, but you did not want it online. They are well liked, and you started the job two weeks ago.

options.text: Leave it up; a fuss in your second week would sour things.
Comment under it, with a joke, that you would rather not be tagged.
Ask your manager to remind the team of the photo policy.
Ask them privately to take it down, then worry it made you look difficult.

scenario: A hospital has one ventilator left. A 30-year-old has a 60% chance of recovery with it; a 70-year-old who was put on the list first has a 40% chance. The hospital's rule is first come, first served.

options.text: Give it to the 30-year-old.
Give it to the patient who arrived first.

scenario: Someone in your flat keeps eating your yoghurts. You have no proof, but you are 90% sure who it is.

options.text: Plant a disgusting yoghurt at the front of the fridge and wait.
Suggest a shared food budget so everyone pays the same.
Ask them kindly whether they are short on money.
Tell them they owe you the yoghurts and ask them to replace them.

scenario: You can earn a big bonus by persuading a customer to buy an upgrade they do not really need. Nobody would ever find out.

options.text: Make the sale.
Tell them they do not need it.

scenario: You are offered a promotion that would make you the manager of your friends at work.

options.text: Accept; you are the best person for the job.
Accept, but first ask your friends how they feel.
Decline to protect the friendships.
Accept, and use it as a stepping stone to a better company.

scenario: A stranger drops their wallet without noticing and is walking away quickly through a crowd.

answer.prompt: How much effort would you make to return it?

scenario: Your friends plan a weekend trip that you cannot really afford.

options.text: Go anyway and sort out the money later.
Ask the friends who earn more to pay a bigger share, so everyone ends up paying the same effort.
Skip it, and feel left out for weeks.
Go, and quietly let the others cover more of the costs.

scenario: At a dinner, the host proudly serves a dish made from insects. Everyone else is eating it.

options.text: Politely refuse; the idea disgusts you.
Try it out of curiosity.
Eat it so you do not offend the host.
Eat it and post a photo of yourself doing it.

scenario: A stranger is selling the mattress they slept on for five years. It has been professionally cleaned and costs a fifth of the price of a new one.

options.text: Buy the used one.
Pay for a new one.

scenario: A colleague you barely know has seemed upset for weeks but says nothing. Last time you asked someone at work if they were okay, they were offended.

options.text: Ask them gently if they are okay.
Tell your manager so they can step in.
Give them space; it is their business.
Invite them out with the team to cheer them up.

scenario: You come across the public profile of your ex's new partner.

options.text: Look through it, and feel unsettled for the rest of the evening.
Glance at it and move on; it does not bother you.
Look through it to check whether they are better looking than you.
Close it straight away; you decided not to look.

scenario: A self-driving car cannot brake in time. It can hit three pedestrians, or swerve into a wall and kill its only passenger.
A lifeboat is overloaded and will sink in the storm unless one person leaves it.

options.text: Draw lots: nobody's life counts for more than anyone else's.
Volunteer to go yourself.
Make the heaviest person leave to save the rest.
Let the captain decide.

scenario: A fire breaks out. You can reach your own child or a room with five other children, but not both.

options.text: Save your child.
Save the five children.

scenario: Someone cuts in front of you in a long queue.

options.text: Tell them firmly to go to the back.
Let it go; it is only a few minutes.
Step back in front of them without a word.
Make a loud joke about it so others laugh.

scenario: Leaving a car park, you leave a small scratch on a parked car. Nobody saw it. Owning up would cost you your 500-euro insurance excess.

options.text: Leave a note with your phone number.
Drive off; scratches happen.
Wait for the owner to come back.
Drive off, but feel bad about it all day.

scenario: Your team wins an award for a project you led.

answer.prompt: How much of the credit is really yours?

scenario: A friend invites you on a last-minute trip abroad tomorrow, but you planned to finish important work this weekend.

options.text: Go; the work can wait.
Stay and finish the work.
Go, and get more friends to come along.
Stay, and promise your friend a trip next month.

scenario: A friend invites you to stay the night. Their flat is messy and not very clean.

options.text: Stay; the friendship matters more.
Make an excuse and book a hotel.
Stay, and offer to help tidy up.
Tell them honestly that it puts you off.

scenario: Your team of four wins a 2,000 euro bonus. You did about half of the work. Your manager asks you to decide how to split it.

options.text: Split it equally: 500 euros each.
Split it by how much work each person did.
Give a bigger share to the teammate who is short of money.
Take 1,000 euros; the project would have failed without you.
